newsitem.title: UK: Japanese stocks in London flat after U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Japanese stocks in London flat after U.S. data.

text.p: Japanese stocks in London were broadly steady in thin dealings on Friday afternoon as investors sat on the sidelines to assess stronger-than-expected U.S. jobs data and a sharp fall on the Tokyo bourse.
The Nikkei 50 share index in London was up 1.65 points at 1,378.82 at 1325 GMT, little moved by a 227-point fall in the Nikkei index in Tokyo.

"There was very little going on today ahead of the U.S. data. Business centered on selling out of the warrants market as people ironed out positions ahead of the afternoon and weekend," one trader said.

U.S. non-farm payrolls rose 250,000 in August, outstripping expectations of a 244,000 rise. But dealers said the market's reaction was muted as the data failed to send a clear signal on U.S. rate policy.
"As long as the Dow holds steady then there should be no problems and the market should remain stable. There's likely to be more movement on Monday once the data's digested," a second dealer said.
Dealers said selling focused on warrant-related stocks but said pressure was limited, with sentiment helped by the Nikkei in Tokyo holding above the key 20,000-point level.
